body: Family tax credit. Inland Revenue says the full family tax credit for a year is $7,921 for the eldest child and $6,454 for every other child. If family income is over $44,900, Inland Revenue works out abatement by subtracting $44,900 from family income and multiplying the difference by 27.5%.

In-work tax credit. Inland Revenue says that from 1 April 2026 the maximum weekly in-work tax credit increases from $97 to $147, and the maximum yearly amount increases from $5,070 to $7,670. After 31 March 2027, the maximum entitlement returns to $97 a week, $5,070 a year. If a family has 1, 2, or 3 children, the full-year in-work tax credit is $7,670 during the increase period. If the family has 4 or more children, it is $7,670 for the first 3 children plus $780 for every child after that. For income over $44,900, the abatement rate is 27.5%.

Best Start. Inland Revenue says that from 1 April 2026, for children born on or after 1 April 2026, the weekly payment of $77 is reduced when family income exceeds $79,000. The annual amount is up to $4,041. For children born before 1 April 2026, from 1 April 2026 the amount increases to $77 a week, up to $4,041, with different first-year abatement timing.

Minimum family tax credit. Inland Revenue says the minimum family tax credit tops up qualifying working families to $36,604 a year after tax, or $703 a week. Examples calculate full-year entitlement as $36,604 minus family income after tax.
